newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say PM nomination changes nothing.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say PM nomination changes nothing.

text.p: Zairean rebels said on Wednesday the nomination of Etienne Tshisekedi by the opposition in Kinshasa as new prime minister made no difference to their goal.

"It won't make any difference. Our purpose is to get rid of (President) Mobutu (Sese Seko) and we will push until we have got him out," Mwenze Kongolo, justice commissioner in the rebel alliance, told Reuters.
The opposition in parliament nominated Tshisekedi, Mobutu's arch-foe, on Tuesday as the new prime minister to steer Zaire through negotiations with the rebels, who hold a quarter of the country.
Many Zairean politicians said they expected ailing Mobutu to move quickly to sign Tshisekedi's appointment into law to succeed prime minister Kengo wa Dondo, who resigned a week ago.
The rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Cong-Zaire warned Tshisekedi against taking the job, arguing anyone under Mobutu can play no part in a rebel-led transitional government.

Presidential Movement leader Idambituo Bakata indicated on Tuesday that Mobutu would endorse the appointment of the man he sacked as prime minister in 1992. A sovereign conference reappointed Tshisekedi but Mobutu again dismissed him in 1993.
Tshisekedi, 64, has huge popular support in Zaire but support for rebel leader Laurent Kabila has also grown in the face of rebel advances since October against the Zairean army.
